text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Judgment to be given on Monday by a court martial in case in which nine air force officers are charged with embezzling 63 million naira.
- Shell awards 26 billion naira contract for a gas plant.
- A 1.1 billion naira scam at Federal Environmental Protection Agency
- Onitsha inland port in eastern Nigeria idle 13 years after it was opened, investigations show.
- Nigerian Stock Exchange protests to the presidency over comments by Finance Minister Anthony Ani that it is unimaginative and unaccountable.
- Kabo Airline and Quantum Management and Enterprises Limited pump 45 million naira each into Broad Bank, acquiring 60 percent equity in the bank.
- Transport minister Major-General Ibrahim Gumel urges the numerous shipping companies in Nigeria to merge in order to strengthen their bases.
- A 19-member Taiwanese trade delegation is expected in Nigeria on Thursday.

- President of Nigerian-American chamber of commerce and industry Moses Ihonde says the group plans to initiate dialogue between Nigerian government and the United States to end current face-off between Washington and Abuja.
- Nigerian Liquefied Natural Gas (NLNG) plans to raise eight billion naira from local banks to part finance its $4 billion project to build a gas plant in southeastern Nigeria.
- Finance Minister Anthony Ani is to brief International Monetary Fund and World Bank in Washington next week on Nigeria's privatisation agenda for next year.
